rationale: Real HTTP/store integration protects asynchronous automatic delivery, idempotency and refusal boundaries.

cases.title: delivers a committed send before the next poll without waiting in the HTTP handler
cases.reason: Deferred real store claim proves the HTTP response completes before provider delivery and the next poll.

cases.title: keeps concurrent accepted retries idempotent while automatic delivery runs
cases.reason: Concurrent identical send requests produce one durable message and one automatic delivery.

cases.title: does not wake for invalid, unowned or dead registrations
cases.reason: Invalid input, wrong ownership and a dead registration leave the wake callback unused.

cases.title: does not wake a refused %s send
cases.reason: Store errors and rate-limit refusals stop automatic work at the HTTP boundary.

cases.title: preserves dismissal of an already %s alert
cases.reason: Both queued and delivered alerts retain the durable dismissal result during automatic delivery.

rationale: SQLite uniqueness and independent PostgreSQL opens prove actual durable session/schema race behavior.

cases.title: serializes sessions on SQLite
cases.reason: Twenty real SQLite session creations leave one live credential.

cases.title: enforces one session per host directly in the schema
cases.reason: A direct duplicate insert is rejected by the actual unique host-session index.

cases.title: leaves exactly one live token after concurrent creates
cases.reason: Independent PostgreSQL session creates leave exactly one live token and row.

cases.title: allows concurrent schema startup
cases.reason: Four independent PostgreSQL opens apply the schema without a startup race.

rationale: Validation mode uses actual read-only PostgreSQL privileges and suppresses mutation consumers.

cases.title: fails closed on an invalid validation mode
cases.reason: Invalid validation-mode strings fail configuration parsing rather than enabling writes.

cases.title: validation cannot write PostgreSQL and starts no consumers or pruners
cases.reason: Actual read-only PostgreSQL credentials reject writes despite hostile URL options; validation serves health but refuses mutations and starts no consumers.

rationale: Deferred real SQLite transactions prove serialization and recovery after failure.

cases.title: releases queued work and close after a SQLite transaction cannot acquire its lock
cases.reason: A native SQLite BEGIN blocked by another connection fails, then queued work and database close complete.

cases.title: does not roll back a transaction when BEGIN failed before taking ownership
cases.reason: A failed nested BEGIN leaves the already-owned SQLite transaction intact instead of rolling it back.

rationale: The real broker HTTP app protects route authorization, durable operation identity and error responses.

cases.title: runs only after acquiring the durable lease
cases.reason: The broker obtains a durable mutation lease before invoking supersession and releases it after success.

cases.title: rejects a commit not bound to the immutable image
cases.reason: An immutable-image commit mismatch rejects the request before acquiring a lease or running a mutation.

cases.title: retains the lease when supersession fails
cases.reason: A failed supersession retains its durable lease for controlled recovery.

cases.title: passes exact completed-attempt and live-lease recovery pins
cases.reason: Completed-attempt identifiers and object-generation pins cross the HTTP-to-runner boundary unchanged.

cases.title: conditionally resumes the exact live supersession lease
cases.reason: An authorized recovery request supplies the exact live generation, operation and request digest to lease acquisition.

cases.title: rejects a live supersession lease for another operation
cases.reason: Recovery naming a different operation cannot take over a live lease.

cases.title: fences the configured source only after acquiring the durable lease
cases.reason: Source fencing acquires its durable lease before running the configured-source operation.

cases.title: rejects duplicate targets and the configured source
cases.reason: Duplicate target IDs and the source cell itself are refused before any fence operation.

cases.title: retains the source-fence lease after a controlled failure
cases.reason: A controlled source-fence failure retains the recovery lease.

rationale: Command ordering and flag-value associations now prove the actual fence invocation rather than an unordered string inventory.

cases.title: passes distinct read and mutation identity tokens
cases.reason: Distinct identity tokens reach their separate child-process environment variables while unrelated environment survives.

cases.title: binds a source fence to deterministic targets and the production var file
cases.reason: Use unsorted targets and assert each value immediately follows its flag; unordered string membership could accept swapped values and never exercised sorting.

rationale: Conditional object-store writes protect lease ownership; live takeover mismatch coverage now independently varies all three identity fields.

cases.title: creates and conditionally releases a new lease
cases.reason: The emitted GCS create and delete URLs require generations zero and seven respectively.

cases.title: rejects a different request while the durable lease is live
cases.reason: A different live request fails before any upload can replace the durable lease.

cases.title: takes over an expired lease with an exact generation precondition
cases.reason: Expired takeover pins the upload to the generation actually read.

cases.title: conditionally replaces the exact authorized live lease
cases.reason: Authorized live takeover pins the replacement upload to the exact inspected generation.

cases.title: rejects a live-lease takeover when any expected field differs
cases.reason: Exercise generation, operationId and requestDigest mismatches independently; the old title promised all three but only changed generation.

rationale: Actual admin HTTP routes distinguish transient database pressure from permanent request/store errors.

cases.title: answers cell-status with a retryable 503 instead of a not-found
cases.reason: A pool-pressure error becomes retryable 503 on the actual cell-status route.

cases.title: keeps the not-found mapping for a real cell-status failure
cases.reason: A genuine missing-cell error retains its distinct not-found HTTP response.

cases.title: answers admission-selector/status with a retryable 503 instead of a conflict
cases.reason: Pool pressure becomes retryable 503 rather than selector conflict.

cases.title: keeps the conflict mapping for a real admission-selector/status failure
cases.reason: A genuine selector conflict retains its conflict HTTP response.

cases.title: leaves the pre-request guards ahead of the mapping alone
cases.reason: Role, authentication and schema guards reject requests before database-error mapping runs.

rationale: Independent authorization fixtures replace imported production allowlists, so widening a dedicated identity policy can fail its tests.

cases.title: allows the staging capacity identity only its transition routes
cases.reason: Use independent expected capacity permissions and denied mutations; importing the production allowlist made privilege expansion self-validating.

cases.title: allows the Asia proof identity only its selector and status routes
cases.reason: Use independent Asia-proof permissions and the real additive-selector route in negative authorization checks.

cases.title: keeps the monitor identity on exact aggregate read routes
cases.reason: Use independent aggregate-read expectations and denial exceptions, including host-whereabouts restrictions across identities.

cases.title: allows only reviewed fence evidence mutations beyond aggregate reads
cases.reason: Pin the fence identity to independently specified inspection reads and deny all unrelated mutations; correct the misleading mutation title.

cases.title: allows the broker only exact fence inspection and mutation routes
cases.reason: Pin broker mutation and inspection permissions independently, so adding a forbidden route in production fails denial checks.

cases.title: rejects unknown routes for dedicated identities
cases.reason: Dedicated identities reject unknown admin routes and non-admin paths without relying on exported policy arrays.

rationale: Independent PostgreSQL connections exercise admission races, query plans and debt reconciliation. Teardown now removes its aborted migration so repeated runs do not fail on the next insert.

cases.title: commits only one parallel assignment at the admission boundary
cases.reason: Independent PostgreSQL stores race at the final connection slot and only one transaction commits.

cases.title: uses the composite headroom index when released history dominates
cases.reason: EXPLAIN over 50,000 released reservations verifies the real composite index avoids scanning history.

cases.title: deduplicates expired debt after a fresh PostgreSQL snapshot
cases.reason: A fresh absolute PostgreSQL snapshot releases only redundant expired debt.

cases.title: releases an aborted older epoch after a fresh PostgreSQL snapshot
cases.reason: A fresh PostgreSQL snapshot retires debt belonging to a proven aborted older epoch. Repeated execution exposed a leaked aborted migration; teardown now removes that durable fixture row.

rationale: Real SQLite assignments and connection telemetry protect capacity, durable reservation debt and fail-closed mutation boundaries.

cases.title: requires exact, internally consistent telemetry from limited cells
cases.reason: Malformed or inconsistent limited-cell heartbeat telemetry fails the actual store admission boundary.

cases.title: reports the limited-cell capacity contract and telemetry components
cases.reason: Real SQLite deployment status combines configured limits with heartbeat ledger components.

cases.title: fails placement closed while a cell changes connection limits
cases.reason: Changing limits through reconciliation invalidates placement until fresh matching telemetry arrives.

cases.title: fails placement closed while the admin path changes connection limits
cases.reason: Changing limits through the admin configuration entrypoint also invalidates stale telemetry.

cases.title: admits exactly one reservation at the admission boundary
cases.reason: Only the last permitted pending reservation is admitted at the connection boundary.

cases.title: rejects at the boundary before mutating durable assignment state
cases.reason: A refusal leaves assignment rows, epochs and reservations unchanged in SQLite.

cases.title: charges every active reservation state at the admission boundary
cases.reason: Reserved, claimed and late-arrival debt each consume admission headroom.

cases.title: does not charge released reservation history
cases.reason: Released reservation history consumes no current admission capacity.

cases.title: rejects sticky control restoration before mutating assignment state
cases.reason: Restoring a sticky control at the connection boundary fails before durable mutation.

cases.title: moves a zero-activity assignment off a general cell without connection headroom
cases.reason: An idle general-cell host can move when restoring control has no headroom.

cases.title: keeps non-control activity pinned when its cell has no connection headroom
cases.reason: Non-control activity preserves the pin rather than permitting an unsafe capacity-driven move.

cases.title: keeps a zero-activity assignment pinned on an existing-only cell
cases.reason: An existing-only pin cannot be escaped solely because control restoration has no headroom.

cases.title: keeps a zero-activity assignment pinned on an unstamped migration-only cell
cases.reason: An unstamped migration-only pin remains authoritative under connection pressure.

cases.title: renames a pending reservation exactly once on control activation
cases.reason: Repeated control activation converts one pending reservation to one claim without duplication.

cases.title: keeps expired pending reservations charged as late-arrival debt
cases.reason: Expired pending controls remain charged as late-arrival debt until independently reconciled.

cases.title: reconciles late-arrival debt only after a covering absolute snapshot
cases.reason: Debt is released only after a fresh absolute snapshot covers the claimed inclusion watermark.

cases.title: rejects duplicate and out-of-order absolute snapshots
cases.reason: Duplicate and older absolute snapshots cannot regress connection accounting.

cases.title: keeps crash retries bound to one reservation claim
cases.reason: Crash/retry activation reuses the durable reservation claim instead of minting debt again.

cases.title: releases only redundant expired debt after a fresh absolute snapshot
cases.reason: Only redundant expired debt is retired after the covering snapshot; live reservations remain.

cases.title: releases expired debt for a snapshot-proven aborted older epoch
cases.reason: Snapshot-proven older aborted epochs release their debt without touching current claims.

cases.title: fails a limited cell closed on stale telemetry while leaving legacy cells unchanged
cases.reason: Stale telemetry refuses limited cells while legacy uncapped cells retain admission.

cases.title: does not create connection debt for mixed-version uncapped cells
cases.reason: Mixed-version uncapped cells create no connection-reservation rows.

cases.title: rejects dormant rebalance before changing the assignment epoch
cases.reason: A dormant rebalance cannot advance its epoch when target headroom is exhausted.

cases.title: rejects an evacuation target at its pause before migration mutation
cases.reason: Evacuation at the target pause fails before any migration or assignment mutation.

rationale: Real PostgreSQL supersession retains authority and accounting under a stale control epoch.

cases.title: serializes parallel generations into one durable control
cases.reason: Parallel control generations across independent PostgreSQL stores converge on one lease and exact assignment/cell counters, including seeded older controls.

rationale: Dead reserve-cell recovery and fence evidence use real PostgreSQL state and independent connections rather than mocked decisions.

cases.title: §8a: the dead-man re-registered the hosts (rows + leases), then the cell died: they move, epoch+1, leases gone
cases.reason: Real PostgreSQL rows and re-registered leases move only the requesting host, advance its epoch and clear obsolete accounting.

cases.title: hard crash with no dead-man trip: a ledger-only row moves too
cases.reason: A ledger-only host row recovers after a hard crash without inventing a source activity lease.

cases.title: a seat ahead of the row: the move mints above it, and the revived cell's seat never wins the row back
cases.reason: A seat ahead of the ledger raises the replacement epoch floor; the revived cell cannot reclaim authority.

cases.title: without the step-5 plan's epoch floor (placement off), the fence is kept
cases.reason: Omitting the step-five epoch floor preserves the durable fence requirement.

cases.title: a withheld verdict (fleet or region guard) keeps the fence
cases.reason: Withheld fleet and region verdicts preserve the fence despite stale heartbeat evidence.

cases.title: a cell heartbeating but not ready keeps its hosts, however long its polls fail
cases.reason: Fresh not-ready heartbeat blocks reassignment even after a continuous poll failure streak.

cases.title: drain then death keeps the fence: a disabled cell is draining, not unheard
cases.reason: Disabled/draining cells retain the fence rather than being mistaken for crashed reserve cells.

cases.title: LB drain: heartbeat fresh while polls fail, so the host is pinned to its cell
cases.reason: Fresh heartbeat evidence prevents load-balancer poll failures alone from moving a host.

cases.title: DB outage or director freeze: heartbeat stale but polls answered (no verdict), so 503
cases.reason: Stale heartbeat without an unanswered-poll verdict refuses recovery instead of guessing death.

cases.title: a sweep (not the host asking) keeps requiring the fence
cases.reason: Background evacuation cannot use the host-request-only exception to fencing.

cases.title: reserve only: a capped db-mode cell keeps the fence (autoheal returns it with its hosts)
cases.reason: Capped database-mode cells retain fencing because autoheal may restore their live hosts.

cases.title: a post-drain migration pin keeps requiring the fence
cases.reason: Post-drain migration pins override the dead-reserve exception and retain fencing.

rationale: Actual PostgreSQL deployment status aggregates durable assignment, migration and runtime state.

cases.title: classifies pending controls and restart blockers in one PostgreSQL query
cases.reason: Real PostgreSQL aggregation distinguishes pending controls from restart blockers, including malformed units and negative reservation drift.

rationale: Real SQLite query instrumentation proves sticky-cell scope separately from fresh fleet placement without copying SQL text.

cases.title: reads one cell for a sticky assignment even when the capped fleet grows
cases.reason: Real SQLite query results stay scoped to one pinned cell while the fleet grows to 32 limited cells.

cases.title: still considers the full fleet for a new placement
cases.reason: New placement still reads the whole fleet rather than incorrectly using sticky-only scoping.

cases.title: rejects the pinned active host with %s
cases.reason: Freshness, incarnation and exhausted-headroom inputs each reject a pinned active host.

cases.title: preserves admission for cells without a connection limit
cases.reason: An uncapped legacy cell admits without requiring limited-cell telemetry.

cases.title: counts outstanding reservations at the admission boundary
cases.reason: Outstanding connection reservations close the admission boundary even when runtime load alone appears safe.

rationale: Store and HTTP behavior classify home-cell failures while preserving legacy and mixed-version capacity outcomes.

cases.title: names a readiness failure rather than reporting fleet capacity
cases.reason: A not-ready home cell produces the typed readiness cause instead of fleet-capacity exhaustion.

cases.title: names a heartbeat gap as unheard even though the cell last reported ready
cases.reason: An expired heartbeat produces unheard even when the last heartbeat reported ready.

cases.title: names a drained cell as draining ahead of its heartbeat gap
cases.reason: Disabled admission takes priority over an old heartbeat when naming the drain cause.

cases.title: still reports capacity exhaustion when the fleet has no headroom
cases.reason: A live full fleet still reports capacity exhaustion, preserving the distinct error class.

cases.title: rehomes instead of rejecting when the unavailable cell needs no fence
cases.reason: An uncapped unavailable home may be rehomed through the real store without a fence.

rationale: Concurrent real PostgreSQL re-placement proves accounting and lock ordering. Three fixed sleeps now observe this fixture connection through application_name; release/draining always run in finally.

cases.title: stamps only the named cell on isolate and clears it on restore
cases.reason: Selector updates stamp only the requested isolated cell and clear that stamp on restore.

cases.title: classifies a reconnect by its home cell’s stamp in the verification read
cases.reason: The real verification query classifies a drain return from its home admission row.

cases.title: ignores a stamp older than the roll it is supposed to describe
cases.reason: A roll stamp beyond its age bound cannot trigger reassignment.

cases.title: re-places every host off an isolated cell without leaking a reservation
cases.reason: Fifty real PostgreSQL hosts leave an isolated source with exact durable lease/counter accounting.

cases.title: lets exactly one of a host’s racing dials win the re-placement
cases.reason: Parallel dials for one host commit exactly one replacement epoch and reservation.

cases.title: grants no host the isolated cell after the admission flip commits
cases.reason: After selector commit, new grants never return the isolated cell and later dials remain sticky.

cases.title: leaves the source row to the source’s own releases and keeps the host’s counters
cases.reason: The narrowed placement path preserves source activity and counts rather than prematurely freeing live units.

cases.title: re-places an isolated incumbent while the source row is held
cases.reason: Holding the source cell row cannot block replacement that writes only target rows.

cases.title: waits for the target rows it increments
cases.reason: Observe an actual PostgreSQL target-row lock wait instead of sleeping one second; release held rows in finally and drain the placement task on failure. The observed waiter is restricted to this suite's stores[1] pool application_name, so unrelated suites cannot satisfy the gate.

cases.title: keeps the pin when no general cell in any region has headroom
cases.reason: No general headroom in either region preserves the source pin and accounting.

cases.title: moves to another region when its own is at the connection cap, without the source row
cases.reason: Cross-region replacement avoids the held source row when its home region is full.

cases.title: places a dormant host without asking for its old cell row
cases.reason: A dormant placement does not require locking its previous cell row.

cases.title: leaves a host with leases on two cells to the lease sweep
cases.reason: Aggregate expiry leaves cross-cell leases for the lease-specific sweep.

cases.title: frees the source leases on their own cell when the target dies
cases.reason: A dead replacement target releases each surviving lease against its own original cell.

cases.title: heals counters below the leases on the narrowed path
cases.reason: The narrowed path reconstructs undercounted host counters from durable activity leases.

cases.title: takes the all-rows path for units no lease backs
cases.reason: Unbacked counter units force the full inventory path before being released.

cases.title: refuses at once while the host’s own release holds its assignment row
cases.reason: A held assignment row on an isolated host yields a typed immediate busy refusal.

cases.title: waits up to a second for the row of a host pinned to a live general cell
cases.reason: Observe the real bounded assignment-row wait before releasing the short hold; finally releases it, while the long hold still proves the timeout. The observed waiter is restricted to this suite's stores[1] pool application_name, so unrelated suites cannot satisfy the gate.

cases.title: never waits on the assignment row while its retry holds the pinned cell row
cases.reason: Observe the cell-row retry before acquiring the assignment hold; finally releases both locks, preserving the NOWAIT cycle-prevention proof. The observed waiter is restricted to this suite's stores[1] pool application_name, so unrelated suites cannot satisfy the gate.

rationale: Real SQLite isolates exercise explicit selector stamps, placement and accounting. Removed one duplicate live-cell/no-fence success already covered by a stronger epoch/cell assertion.

cases.title: leaves a host on a live general cell untouched, at one added admission read
cases.reason: A live general pin stays unchanged and pays one indexed admission lookup.

cases.title: keeps a host pinned to a migration-only cell with no roll stamp
cases.reason: Migration-only membership without a current roll stamp cannot move a host.

cases.title: re-places a host once the roll stamp is set
cases.reason: The real selector stamp moves a live host to another cell and advances its epoch; also proves no committed fence is required.

cases.title: treats a stamp $label as $moves
cases.reason: Missing, invalid, stale and current stamp variants exercise actual movement decisions.

cases.title: samples the regional target rows it locks under their own hold site
cases.reason: Replacement locks contribute samples to their distinct hold site rather than fleet inventory.

cases.title: stops re-placing once restore clears the stamp
cases.reason: Restoring general admission clears the stamp and stops subsequent replacement.

cases.title: keeps a host pinned to an existing-only cell that still serves it
cases.reason: Serving existing-only admission preserves the active host pin.

cases.title: keeps a host pinned on an unstamped cell whose migration has completed
cases.reason: A completed migration on an unstamped cell does not itself authorize replacement.

cases.title: re-places a stamped cell whose migration has completed
cases.reason: A completed migration no longer blocks movement when a current isolate stamp exists.

cases.title: keeps the pin while a migration lease is outstanding
cases.reason: An outstanding migration lease still owns the host epoch and prevents movement.

cases.title: keeps the pin while a migration row is open but its lease has lapsed
cases.reason: An open durable migration row continues to block movement after its activity lease expires.

cases.title: crosses a region boundary only when its own region has no room
cases.reason: Other-region fallback occurs only after exhausting same-region general capacity.

cases.title: keeps the pin, and says so, when no region has a general cell with room
cases.reason: Exhausting both regions keeps the pin and emits the precise defer reason.

cases.title: prefers its own region over a less loaded cell elsewhere
cases.reason: A home-region target wins over a less-loaded foreign region.

cases.title: moves the only cell of a region to another region
cases.reason: A region with only the isolated source can place its host in another region.

cases.title: books the reserve cell before leaving the region, and the canary still counts the move
cases.reason: An available in-region reserve booking occurs before foreign spill and emits the committed canary move.

cases.title: leaves the region as before when the reserve cell has no room either
cases.reason: A full reserve target permits ordinary foreign-region fallback.

cases.title: treats a throttled reserve cell as no room, so the drain does not wait on its intake
cases.reason: Reserve intake throttling is treated as no room so drain return does not wait on rate limiting.

cases.title: counts a share-draw booking off the isolated cell for the canary
cases.reason: A share-draw reserve placement still emits the committed isolate-replacement canary.

cases.title: does not hold a host whose preferred region is elsewhere
cases.reason: An explicitly different region preference does not unnecessarily retain the source pin.

cases.title: takes the dead-cell path when a stamped cell stops heartbeating
cases.reason: A stamped cell with an expired heartbeat follows dead-cell fencing rather than live replacement.

cases.title: does not demand a committed fence while the stamped cell is live
cases.reason: Remove this replay: the earlier roll-stamp case already assigns successfully without installing any committed fence and checks the epoch/cell change.

cases.title: leaves the source cell activity leases in place
cases.reason: Live source activity remains on its original cell after replacement.

cases.title: emits nothing when the placement rolls back after the decision
cases.reason: An injected post-decision write failure rolls back placement and emits no committed-move log.

cases.title: logs one event naming both cells, the admission state and the region
cases.reason: A committed move logs both cells, regions and admission state without host identities.

cases.title: is left to the lease sweep by aggregate expiry
cases.reason: Aggregate expiry does not release retained source leases against the replacement cell.

cases.title: frees the source leases on their own cell when the target dies
cases.reason: Dead-target cleanup releases source leases against their original accounting rows.

cases.title: retries a busy isolated attempt in its own tier, never under the all-rows lock
cases.reason: A busy narrowed attempt retries within its isolated tier instead of widening to all cell rows.

cases.title: marks the host only while the roll stamp is current
cases.reason: Verification marks a drain return only while the roll stamp remains current.

cases.title: does not mark a host parked without a stamp or held by a migration
cases.reason: Unstamped parking and outstanding migration ownership prevent drain-return classification.

cases.title: reads the classification in the verification query itself
cases.reason: Classification is returned by the verification query, avoiding a second admission read.

cases.title: still treats a host its draining cell already released as a drain return
cases.reason: A source-side release does not erase a still-current drain-return classification.

rationale: Reserve-mode evacuation protects actual migration ordering and mixed admission behavior.

cases.title: completes no evacuation from a reserve source, though it holds no source lease
cases.reason: A reserve source's absent database leases cannot make its evacuation appear ready to complete.

cases.title: refuses evacuation status for a reserve cell, where activeCellMigrations would count no units
cases.reason: Status rejects reserve source and target cells rather than reporting misleading zero activity.

rationale: Independent PostgreSQL operations protect reserve admission and durable counters under concurrency.

cases.title: flips a cell to reserve and back, and refuses reserve while a migration names it
cases.reason: Actual PostgreSQL admit-mode transitions refuse reserve when an active migration references the cell.

cases.title: pins a host on a live reserve cell without writing its rows, and re-places it once that cell is dead
cases.reason: A live reserve pin is returned without row writes, then moves after independent death evidence.

cases.title: does not re-place a host off a reserve cell that heartbeats while not ready
cases.reason: Not-ready but heartbeating reserve cells keep their existing host assignment.

cases.title: places a fresh host on a reserve cell only while its own current-process row says db
cases.reason: Fresh placement uses the cell's current-process admit-effective row and rejects stale-incarnation state.

cases.title: assigns while the admit-mode read times out (57014), without aborting the transaction
cases.reason: A real 57014 read timeout occurs outside the placement transaction, which can still commit.

cases.title: reads the reserve set once for concurrent assigns during a stall, and not again in the backoff
cases.reason: Concurrent assigns share one stalled reserve-set read and honor its post-failure backoff.

rationale: Actual SQLite state and reserve wire boundaries prove booking, fallback and refusal behavior.

cases.title: lets no expiry sweep touch a reserve-mode cell, and runs none while the set is unknown
cases.reason: Every expiry sweep skips known reserve cells and pauses while their classification is unknown.

cases.title: logs an unreadable reserve-mode set at most once a minute
cases.reason: An unreadable reserve table produces at most one warning per minute on the injected clock.

cases.title: tells break glass whether a cell is still heartbeating
cases.reason: Heartbeat freshness is exposed independently for break-glass operations.

cases.title: keeps an idle host sticky on a reserve-mode cell where today it would be re-placed
cases.reason: An idle reserve host remains sticky despite ordinary dormancy rules.

cases.title: keeps a connected host pinned when its reserve cell goes existing-only after a ledger write
cases.reason: A connected reserve host stays pinned after an existing-only admission ledger update.

cases.title: reads afresh after an admit-mode write instead of joining a read begun before it
cases.reason: An admit-mode write invalidates an already-running read instead of joining stale results.

cases.title: does not back off for a pre-write read that fails after the write
cases.reason: Failure of a read begun before the write cannot impose backoff on the new generation.

cases.title: checks pins and dormancy against the last-known set once the read goes stale
cases.reason: The last-known reserve set still protects pins and dormancy while its refresh is stale.

cases.title: never places a fresh host on a reserve-mode cell through the database
cases.reason: Fresh database placement excludes reserve-mode cells.

cases.title: refuses drains, evacuations and status reads that would treat a reserve-mode cell as empty
cases.reason: Drain, evacuation and aggregate status refuse reserve cells instead of treating absent leases as empty.

cases.title: refuses the flip to reserve while a migration names the cell
cases.reason: A migration referencing the cell prevents switching its admission to reserve.

rationale: Separate PostgreSQL sessions distinguish assignment and inventory lock ordering during concurrent work.

cases.title: runs the cell accept and the placement retry concurrently without a cycle
cases.reason: Twelve waves of concurrent accept/release and placement retry use independent PostgreSQL stores; actual database deadlock counters remain zero.

rationale: Focused boundary fakes inspect lock options/order while executing the real store; real PostgreSQL suites supply concurrency coverage.

cases.title: updates the cell only after assignment activity during release
cases.reason: Recording a real SQLite release proves assignment/activity changes precede the cell counter write.

cases.title: updates the cell only after inserting new activity
cases.reason: New activity is inserted under host locks before its cell reservation changes.

cases.title: rechecks an expired candidate after taking the assignment lock
cases.reason: Expired candidates are rechecked after the assignment lock, preventing deletion based on an unlocked snapshot.

cases.title: fails fast before aggregate cleanup waits on mixed-version assignment rows
cases.reason: Aggregate cleanup requests NOWAIT before crossing mixed-version assignment-row lock order.

cases.title: releases the placement capacity lock before heartbeat reservation cleanup
cases.reason: Heartbeat cleanup starts only after releasing its cell-capacity transaction.

cases.title: does not let an old heartbeat clean replacement-incarnation reservations
cases.reason: An old-incarnation heartbeat cannot retire a replacement process's outstanding reservations.

cases.title: locks only general-admission inventory for a brand-new assignment
cases.reason: Brand-new placement locks only general-admission inventory.

cases.title: keeps a brand-new assignment retry scoped to general admission
cases.reason: A first lock failure retries new placement without widening beyond general admission.

cases.title: restarts with full inventory if an assignment appears during a general retry
cases.reason: An assignment appearing between retries forces the wider inventory path before mutation.

cases.title: probes the sticky cell before locking full inventory for dead-cell reassignment
cases.reason: Dead reassignment probes the pinned cell before taking fleet inventory.

cases.title: locks host rows first and the target cell row last, NOWAIT, with no fleet-wide lock
cases.reason: A real idle-rehome commit locks host rows first and only its final target row NOWAIT, preserving the cross-path deadlock argument.

cases.title: keeps the target-row lock clause when a wrapper omits the dialect
cases.reason: An omitted dialect wrapper retains the embedded target-row NOWAIT clause rather than silently unlocking it.

rationale: One hundred and one individual real SQLite cases protect assignment lifecycle, migration authority, reservation accounting and durable refusal behavior.

cases.title: admits only cells with a fresh ready heartbeat
cases.reason: Real SQLite heartbeat expiry/readiness boundaries decide which configured cells admit assignments.

cases.title: fences stale incarnations and origin mismatches
cases.reason: Wrong cell origin and stale process incarnation cannot overwrite current heartbeat authority.

cases.title: records receipt-relative legacy drain states and pins post-send migrations
cases.reason: A real drain send/receipt state machine preserves receipt-relative grace and pins migrations after send.

cases.title: recovers a proven drain once after the source cell is replaced
cases.reason: Recovery after source replacement is durable and idempotent and requires the proven drain evidence.

cases.title: rejects an invalid receipt and a prepared drain from an old incarnation
cases.reason: Invalid receipt fields and a drain prepared for an obsolete source incarnation are rejected.

cases.title: restores an expired registered migration lease before a prepared drain send
cases.reason: A registered migration's expired activity lease is reconstructed before sending a prepared drain.

cases.title: refreshes registered migration leases before prepared drain recovery
cases.reason: Prepared drain recovery refreshes registered migration lease/accounting before proceeding.

cases.title: bounds repeated accounting repair before prepared drain recovery
cases.reason: Repeated accounting drift cannot trigger an unbounded repair loop during drain recovery.

cases.title: retires a pinned migration superseded by a newer authoritative assignment
cases.reason: A newer authoritative assignment retires obsolete pinned migration data without corrupting its current cell.

cases.title: refuses to restore a missing migration lease without durable target registration
cases.reason: Unregistered targets cannot supply the durable evidence needed to restore a missing migration lease.

cases.title: moves a dead assignment only after a completed exact-incarnation fence attempt
cases.reason: A legacy attestation alone does not move a dead capped host; a completed exact-incarnation Terraform attempt does.

cases.title: preserves proven non-delivery and permits one fresh full-grace attempt
cases.reason: Proof of non-delivery permits a fresh full-grace drain instead of consuming its delivery budget.

cases.title: binds fence attestation to one durable Terraform attempt
cases.reason: Every Terraform evidence field, plan generation and GCE operation remains bound to one durable attempt across retries.

cases.title: aborts only a Terraform fence whose apply never started
cases.reason: Only an attempt whose apply never started can be aborted; later apply is refused.

cases.title: adopts a stale disabled legacy fence only when no durable attempt exists
cases.reason: Legacy adoption requires stale disabled runtime, records explicit commit, refreshes idempotently and is cleared by heartbeat.

cases.title: rejects legacy adoption after a %s durable attempt
cases.reason: Active, completed and aborted durable attempts each forbid legacy adoption.

cases.title: serializes legacy adoption against durable attempt preparation
cases.reason: Concurrent SQLite adoption/preparation produce one winner and mutually exclusive durable evidence.

cases.title: rejects an expired durable Terraform fence attempt
cases.reason: Preparation TTL expiry prevents starting an old Terraform apply.

cases.title: keeps a started Terraform fence attempt recoverable after its preparation TTL
cases.reason: An apply started before TTL remains recoverable afterwards and cannot be replaced with different evidence.

cases.title: reports aggregate deployment state and heartbeat freshness without identities
cases.reason: Deployment status aggregates real counts/freshness and excludes assignment identities from the returned shape.

cases.title: keeps concurrent sticky assignment grants restart-safe
cases.reason: Twenty sticky grants leave one pending control and no spurious restart blocker.

cases.title: classifies activated and non-control activity as restart-blocking
cases.reason: Activated control and all non-control activity kinds contribute the expected restart-blocking units.

cases.title: fails closed for malformed pending controls and unexplained reservations
cases.reason: Malformed pending-control units and positive/negative reservation drift remain visible as blockers.

cases.title: keeps a migration blocking when its target also has a pending control
cases.reason: A pending target control does not hide the migration's restart-blocking activity.

cases.title: starts declared candidates disabled without overwriting later operator state
cases.reason: Initially-disabled candidates stay disabled until explicit operator enablement, which reconciliation preserves.

cases.title: moves a stranded host off an existing-only cell that stopped serving it
cases.reason: A recent unanswered existing-only grant escapes after the stranded age, and later grants stay on its replacement.

cases.title: keeps a serving existing-only cell pinned for hosts with live activity
cases.reason: A live claimed control proves an existing-only cell still serves its host and keeps it pinned.

cases.title: keeps migration-only cells pinned inside the stranded window
cases.reason: Migration-only admission alone does not authorize moving a recently active host.

cases.title: leaves quiet existing-only assignments to the normal dormancy rule
cases.reason: Quiet existing-only hosts outside the stranded window keep the ordinary dormancy pin.

cases.title: reassigns an active assignment from an uncapped stale cell without a fence
cases.reason: Uncapped dead-cell recovery advances the epoch and removes obsolete migrations, pins and source activity.

cases.title: skips a host whose row is busy and still evacuates the rest of the dead cell
cases.reason: A typed busy error on the first host does not prevent evacuating later eligible hosts.

cases.title: does not let an unfenced capped cell starve eligible legacy recovery
cases.reason: An unfenced capped host does not starve an eligible legacy host when the sweep limit is one.

cases.title: refuses evacuation into a cell without a fresh ready heartbeat
cases.reason: Evacuation refuses a target without fresh ready heartbeat evidence.

cases.title: keeps an active assignment sticky without increasing its epoch or reservation
cases.reason: Repeated active assignment returns the same grant without increasing reservations or epoch.

cases.title: selects the least-loaded cell with a stable cell-id tie break
cases.reason: Least-loaded selection and deterministic cell-ID tie breaking distribute two real assignments.

cases.title: admits exactly through the configured capacity boundary
cases.reason: A third assignment at two-unit capacity is refused without increasing the cell counter.

cases.title: does not oversubscribe when assignments race
cases.reason: Eight racing SQLite assigns admit exactly the configured two units.

cases.title: reassigns only after all activity expires and the dormant TTL elapses
cases.reason: Reassignment waits for both expired activity and the dormancy interval before advancing the epoch.

cases.title: will not normally move an assignment while any durable activity remains
cases.reason: Remaining durable migration activity prevents ordinary dormancy-based reassignment.

cases.title: releases every expired activity reservation without going negative
cases.reason: Lease-specific and aggregate expiry release all activity classes exactly once without negative accounting.

cases.title: isolates assignments by host and verifies both cell and epoch
cases.reason: Host identity, assigned cell and epoch are all required for verification and resolution.

cases.title: converts the director reservation into an idempotent active-control lease
cases.reason: Repeated activation converts one pending grant to one durable control lease.

cases.title: transactionally supersedes older controls on only the same cell
cases.reason: Same-cell older controls are superseded transactionally while source-cell activity remains counted.

cases.title: re-reserves a sticky grant for a host holding no control lease
cases.reason: A sticky host with no control lease receives one fresh pending reservation.

cases.title: re-pins a host that took control after the sticky lane read it dormant
cases.reason: Activity inserted between sticky and placement lanes restores the pin and preserves exact counters/lease expiry.

cases.title: reserves control on the pinned cell when the only lease sits on another
cases.reason: A control lease on another cell cannot satisfy the current pinned cell's pending reservation.

cases.title: mints a pending control when the only lease is an older epoch pending
cases.reason: A pending lease for an old epoch cannot satisfy the authoritative epoch's new pending grant.

cases.title: re-reserves a re-pinned grant for a host holding no control lease
cases.reason: A splice appearing between lanes preserves its reservation and adds exactly one pending control.

cases.title: extends the lease of a control-holding host on a sticky grant
cases.reason: Sticky control grants extend durable lease expiry and last-activity timestamps.

cases.title: never shortens a migration lease to the grant lease
cases.reason: Touching a migrated host never shortens its longer migration lease to the ordinary grant TTL.

cases.title: moves an origin-scoped activity reservation without double counting
cases.reason: Moving one origin-scoped activity releases its old units and charges its new cell only once.

cases.title: rejects a durable activity before it can exceed cell capacity
cases.reason: An over-capacity durable splice fails before changing existing reservation accounting.

cases.title: moves active assignments target-first and completes only after source drain
cases.reason: Target-first evacuation requires registration and source release, then refuses late source activity.

cases.title: automatically completes only after the source runtime is freshly quiescent
cases.reason: Automatic completion requires freshly quiescent source runtime and current target incarnation activation.

cases.title: completes a fenced migration only after the source heartbeat is stale
cases.reason: Fenced completion waits for stale source heartbeat rather than trusting a live source fence request.

cases.title: logs the drift reconciliation corrects, once, after it commits
cases.reason: Reservation drift logs only the correction that committed and does not repeat once accounting is healed.

cases.title: blocks aggregate fenced completion on assignment accounting mismatch
cases.reason: Assignment counter mismatch prevents aggregate fenced completion.

cases.title: blocks aggregate fenced completion on an unexpected third-cell lease
cases.reason: Unexpected activity on a third cell prevents aggregate fenced completion.

cases.title: rolls back an unregistered expired evacuation with a strictly newer epoch
cases.reason: Expired unregistered evacuation rolls back with a strictly newer epoch and frees its target units.

cases.title: reaps an expired migration whose registered target cell was disabled
cases.reason: A long-abandoned disabled registered target is retired exactly once.

cases.title: leaves a freshly disabled target for supersede-target to recover
cases.reason: Fresh target disablement retains the operator supersession window until abandonment expires.

cases.title: rolls an abandoned disabled target back while its source remains active
cases.reason: An abandoned target can roll back onto a still-active source without losing its authoritative epoch.

cases.title: starts the abandon window when an old migration target is disabled
cases.reason: Abandonment starts when the target becomes disabled, not at an ancient migration creation time.

cases.title: reaps an expired migration from a retired source when its target control is gone
cases.reason: A retired source with no target control completes on the target and releases stale leases/reservations.

cases.title: reaps a retired-side migration with only a pending target control
cases.reason: A retired-source migration with only expired pending control is completed without carrying ghost reservation units.

cases.title: preserves a fresh target grant created after abandoned migration selection
cases.reason: A fresh target grant inserted after candidate selection survives the reaper and can activate normally.

cases.title: keeps an abandoned target migration open while its source is still active
cases.reason: An active source prevents completing its abandoned target migration.

cases.title: starts the abandon window when an old migration source is retired
cases.reason: Retiring the source starts a new abandonment window rather than reusing old migration age.

cases.title: reaps after an old source migration lease is refreshed and expires
cases.reason: Refreshing then expiring the migration lease still allows legitimate abandoned-state cleanup.

cases.title: keeps a freshly retired target open despite an old retired source
cases.reason: New target retirement gets its own grace window even when source retirement is old.

cases.title: fails supersession closed when reaping wins after selection
cases.reason: Reaping between bulk candidate selection and supersession fails with the specific superseded error.

cases.title: fails supersession closed when reaping wins after preparation
cases.reason: Reaping after supersession preparation still prevents mutating the retired migration.

cases.title: fails supersession closed when reaping wins before an accounting retry
cases.reason: Reaping before a second accounting-repair attempt prevents superseding an obsolete migration.

cases.title: reaps a pinned expired migration once its target cell is disabled
cases.reason: An old post-drain pin does not keep an abandoned disabled target alive forever.

cases.title: repairs an expired migration marker from its exact active target control
cases.reason: An active target control repairs missing registration instead of rolling a live host backward.

cases.title: keeps a registered migration pending while its proven target control is offline
cases.reason: Registered migrations remain pending while their target control is offline and finish after reactivation.

cases.title: completes a registered migration after its disabled source is proven dead
cases.reason: Dead-source completion is idempotent and leaves only the target control reservation.

cases.title: retires an inactive registered migration after its source is proven dead
cases.reason: An inactive target can retire a proven-dead-source migration without keeping pending controls/debt.

cases.title: retires a registered migration and its %s target control after the source dies
cases.reason: Expired and previous-incarnation target controls are both retired after source death without leaving counters or leases.

cases.title: refuses dead-source completion while the source heartbeat is fresh
cases.reason: Fresh source heartbeat rejects fence attestation and dead-source completion before durable mutation.

cases.title: supersedes a registered migration after its disabled target is proven unavailable
cases.reason: Unavailable-target supersession advances authority once, preserves live source control and retires old-target debt.

cases.title: retries registered migration supersession with inventory locked first
cases.reason: An injected inventory NOWAIT failure retries with inventory first and assignment NOWAIT to avoid a lock cycle.

cases.title: reconciles durable cell accounting once before aggregate supersession
cases.reason: Aggregate supersession reconciles corrupted cell counters once before committing the replacement migration.

cases.title: preserves healthy third-cell activity during aggregate supersession
cases.reason: Healthy third-cell activity survives supersession and stays charged to its own cell.

cases.title: refuses supersession while the registered target remains available
cases.reason: A still-available registered target cannot be fenced or superseded and its assignment remains unchanged.

cases.title: serializes concurrent retries of registered migration supersession
cases.reason: Concurrent supersession retries return one replacement and one new durable migration epoch.

cases.title: classifies an expired migration blocked by a newer target assignment
cases.reason: Status explicitly classifies an expired migration whose assignment already advanced on the target.

cases.title: does not complete a registered migration after the assignment epoch advances
cases.reason: Automatic and explicit completion refuse a registered migration whose assignment epoch changed.

cases.title: retires an expired migration without rewriting its newer target assignment
cases.reason: The reaper retires an older migration without rewriting the authoritative newer target assignment or live controls.

cases.title: fails closed when expired migration assignment state is not superseding: $expected
cases.reason: Missing and non-superseding assignment state fail closed and leave the migration open.

cases.title: reconciles duplicated assignment counters and cell reservations after evacuation
cases.reason: Aggregate evacuation reconciliation rebuilds all assignment counters and cell totals from real leases.

cases.title: refuses reservation reconciliation when an activity lease has no assignment
cases.reason: An orphan activity lease prevents reconciliation and leaves cell counters unchanged.

cases.title: refuses reservation reconciliation when an activity lease names no cell
cases.reason: An activity lease naming a missing cell prevents reconciliation without changing existing totals.

cases.title: leaves accounting for cells outside the selected evacuation pair unchanged
cases.reason: Reconciliation of one evacuation pair leaves unrelated third-cell counters untouched.

cases.title: rebalances only a fully inactive assignment after the dormant TTL
cases.reason: Explicit dormant rebalance refuses active control, then advances only after release and dormant TTL.

cases.title: durably removes an unhealthy cell from new assignment without moving existing hosts
cases.reason: Reconciliation preserves an operator-disabled cell; existing hosts remain resolvable while fresh hosts go elsewhere.

cases.title: bulk-migrates active controls without exposing assignment identities
cases.reason: Bulk migration obeys batch limits, reports aggregate diagnostics and completes only after source controls release.

cases.title: skips a batch row that concurrently moved from the selected source to %s
cases.reason: A row concurrently moved to the intended target or a third cell is skipped without creating a migration.

cases.title: does not count an existing migration after a stale batch row moves to its target
cases.reason: A stale selected row whose migration already started is not counted as a new bulk migration.

cases.title: preserves operator-owned tagged URLs and admission state across reconciliation
cases.reason: Operator-owned tagged URLs and disabled admission survive declared topology reconciliation.

cases.title: bulk-migrates activity even when its source control is temporarily absent
cases.reason: A source splice without a control still reserves real migration capacity and can evacuate.

rationale: A throwing cleanup boundary proves later sweeps still run and diagnostics identify the failing step.

cases.title: runs every later sweep when an early one fails, naming the step
cases.reason: A failed first sweep still permits every later cleanup and identifies the failed step in the warning; the stub boundary isolates error handling rather than implementing cleanup.

rationale: Deferred gates prove keyed serialization, unrelated-key concurrency and rejection recovery.

cases.title: serializes operations for the same assignment
cases.reason: Deferred gates prove two operations for the same user and host never overlap.

cases.title: allows different assignments to run concurrently
cases.reason: Distinct users sharing a host id run concurrently, preventing an accidentally global or host-only queue.

cases.title: continues after a rejected operation
cases.reason: A rejected operation releases the assignment queue and the next operation completes.

rationale: Real SQLite diagnostic joins and aggregates preserve missing rows and distinguish reservation states.

cases.title: reports per-cell counters, lease backlog, and reservation debt
cases.reason: Real SQLite joins distinguish expired activity, all lease units, active reservation debt and released history in the reported inventory.

cases.title: reports cells missing runtime and admission rows without failing
cases.reason: Missing admission/runtime rows survive the left joins and produce a usable diagnostic snapshot.

rationale: Real JWT cryptography and host handshakes protect shadow classification, bounded telemetry and continued database authority.

cases.title: names the key by a short hash of it
cases.reason: The public key identifier is a stable short digest of the actual signing key, allowing rotation without exposing the secret.

cases.title: sorts every lease into one class
cases.reason: Real signed JWTs exercise expiration, wrong signature, wrong host/cell/epoch, legacy no-kid compatibility and classification boundaries.

cases.title: does nothing while the switch is off
cases.reason: Disabled shadow checking emits neither counts nor diagnostics.

cases.title: counts each class against the database answer and logs one line per window
cases.reason: Independent lease classes and database outcomes aggregate into one bounded telemetry window and reset after emission.

cases.title: still refuses a host the database refuses, whatever its lease says
cases.reason: A real host handshake remains refused by database authority even with a valid lease.

cases.title: still admits a host the database admits, with no lease at all
cases.reason: A real host handshake succeeds under database authority without a lease, preserving mixed-version compatibility.

rationale: Fake-clock windows retain privacy-safe samples, suppression and bounded eviction. Removed a quiet-key replay already established by the timer-only closure in the first case.

cases.title: emits once per key per window and closes it with its own suppressed count
cases.reason: The first emission, latest sample, suppressed count, timer-only closing emission and next-window reset establish the complete quiet-key behavior.

cases.title: reports the final count for a key that goes quiet
cases.reason: Removed because the preceding case already lets the timer close a quiet key without another rejection and checks its final suppressed count.

cases.title: keeps distinct keys on independent windows
cases.reason: Independent keys close and reset on separate fake-clock windows.

cases.title: bounds the tracked keys and reports what an evicted window suppressed
cases.reason: The 64-key bound evicts an older window and reports its own suppressed count without contaminating other keys.

rationale: Real HTTP boundaries protect actionable failure/grant diagnostics, lane classification and host privacy.

cases.title: logs the store reason and host digest when assign() rejects on capacity
cases.reason: A real HTTP assignment rejection includes the store capacity reason and a digest while withholding the raw host identifier.

cases.title: separates an unavailable home cell from capacity and names its cause
cases.reason: Typed home-cell unavailability survives the HTTP boundary with its specific cause instead of being mislabeled as capacity.

cases.title: logs an unhinted placement rejection without the raw host id
cases.reason: Unhinted placement failures still report their lane and digest without exposing the host id.

cases.title: names the throttled host once per window and closes it with the suppressed count
cases.reason: Fake-clock requests prove per-host rate limiting and a closing suppressed count without a follow-up rejection.

cases.title: stays silent for successful assignments
cases.reason: A successful assignment emits no rejection diagnostic.

cases.title: logs sticky grants with cell id and host digest only
cases.reason: Sticky grants report the selected cell and host digest while excluding the raw host identifier.

cases.title: logs a hinted grant served by the placement lane
cases.reason: A hinted request served by ordinary placement is correctly labeled with its actual lane.

cases.title: does not log unhinted placement grants
cases.reason: Successful unhinted placement avoids grant-log noise.

rationale: Fake-clock retries distinguish transport availability from errors after schema work and enforce a bounded boot budget.

cases.title: waits out a cold proxy instead of failing the boot
cases.reason: Fake-clock transient connection failures eventually recover through the real boot retry loop.

cases.title: fails the boot immediately when the database rejects the relay
cases.reason: A permanent authentication/database rejection fails immediately instead of hiding behind retries.

cases.title: refuses to re-queue the schema apply after SQLSTATE %s
cases.reason: SQLSTATE lock, cancellation and connection-pressure errors after schema execution do not requeue DDL.

cases.title: waits out a connection failure the driver does report a SQLSTATE for
cases.reason: A retryable connection failure carrying SQLSTATE still recovers rather than being mistaken for a schema failure.

cases.title: gives up once the retry budget is spent
cases.reason: The 45-second retry budget bounds cold-start waiting and returns the original failure.

rationale: Real transactional selector state protects exact membership, intent idempotency, compare-and-swap races and legacy safety.

cases.title: preserves sticky assignments while reserving ordinary placement for general cells
cases.reason: Real assignment state keeps sticky existing-only hosts while restricting new ordinary placement to general cells.

cases.title: excludes existing-only and migration-only cells from dormant placement
cases.reason: Dormant placement excludes both existing-only and migration-only cells despite otherwise usable capacity.

cases.title: does not recover an unfenced dead existing-only assignment
cases.reason: A dead existing-only assignment cannot move until fence evidence authorizes recovery.

cases.title: commits atomically and resolves an ambiguous response idempotently
cases.reason: Durable intent, membership, generation and admission state commit together; an ambiguous response replays without another generation.

cases.title: rejects a generation-zero membership change between intent and commit
cases.reason: A generation-zero membership race between durable intent and commit is rejected using the membership fingerprint.

cases.title: preserves admission age for cells unchanged by a selector CAS
cases.reason: Unchanged admission rows retain their original age across a selector compare-and-swap.

cases.title: persists failed CAS intent without mutating current membership
cases.reason: A failed generation compare-and-swap preserves durable intent while leaving active membership untouched.

cases.title: rejects duplicate or incomplete selector membership before mutation
cases.reason: Duplicate and incomplete memberships fail before any selector/admission mutation.

cases.title: inspects an unchanged durable intent after an ambiguous apply failure
cases.reason: An ambiguous failed apply leaves a durable unchanged intent that inspection can classify correctly.

cases.title: allows only one concurrent CAS and never re-enables legacy cells
cases.reason: Concurrent compare-and-swaps elect one winner and later attempts cannot re-enable legacy existing-only cells.

cases.title: preserves the selector boundary across compatible reconciliation
cases.reason: Compatible topology reconciliation preserves the established selector boundary and generation.

cases.title: atomically adds exact migration-only cells after the selector boundary
cases.reason: Adding migration-only cells atomically extends the exact fleet and permits idempotent replay with the same configuration.

cases.title: rejects additive cells before cutover and exact-attempt config reuse
cases.reason: Pre-cutover additions and reuse of an attempt with a different cell configuration fail without partial mutation.

rationale: A real long-held row lock proves startup recovery beyond inner transaction retries; elapsed time is the PostgreSQL boundary under test.

cases.title: recovers after the cell inventory lock outlasts transaction retries
cases.reason: A real PostgreSQL row lock lasts beyond the inner transaction retry budget; outer startup retries recover after release without exhausted-transaction noise.

rationale: Role guards and bounded fake-clock retries exercise actual startup entrypoints rather than configuration inventories.

cases.title: reserves global assignment maintenance for director-capable roles
cases.reason: The maintenance predicate covers director-capable roles and excludes cell-only execution.

cases.title: does not let a cell process reconcile its own admission
cases.reason: The real startup entrypoint refuses cell-side reconciliation before invoking the store.

cases.title: lets the %s process reconcile configured admission without disabling missing cells
cases.reason: Director and combined roles pass their selected configuration through reconciliation without disabling missing cells.

cases.title: waits out transient database pressure during director startup
cases.reason: Fake-clock transient pressure retries then completes director startup.

cases.title: fails startup immediately for a permanent reconciliation error
cases.reason: A permanent reconciliation failure propagates without a retry.

cases.title: bounds transient startup retries
cases.reason: The attempt limit bounds repeated transient startup failures.

cases.title: bounds retry wall time when each reconciliation is slow
cases.reason: A slow reconciliation consumes the wall-time budget, preventing attempts from extending startup indefinitely.

rationale: Deferred write boundaries prove single-flight refresh, owed rollback writes and pool-aware failure recovery.

cases.title: writes on the first tick, on every change, and every 15 s, one write at a time
cases.reason: Deferred database writes prove one write at a time, initial and changed values, and the 15-second refresh boundary.

cases.title: writes nothing while the switch has never said reserve, and one db write on the way out
cases.reason: A never-enabled reserve switch remains write-free; leaving reserve owes one final database-mode write.

cases.title: owes nothing more once a tripped cell already wrote db
cases.reason: A dead-man trip that already wrote database mode does not create another owed write.

cases.title: takes no connection while requests wait for the pool
cases.reason: A busy request pool prevents the background writer from acquiring another connection.

cases.title: retries a failed write on the next tick and rate-limits its log line
cases.reason: A failed write retries on the next tick while its warning obeys a separate rate limit.

rationale: A real TCP proxy validates lazy boot and readiness recovery during an actual PostgreSQL wire outage.

cases.title: listens with /health 200 and /ready 503, then turns ready once the database answers
cases.reason: A real TCP proxy outage permits lazy cell boot and HTTP health while readiness fails; restoring the PostgreSQL wire turns readiness healthy.

rationale: Independent PostgreSQL sessions race two mutually exclusive durable operations.

cases.title: allows either adoption or attempt preparation, never both
cases.reason: Separate PostgreSQL connections race adoption against attempt preparation and durable state proves the mutually exclusive winner.

rationale: Actual outbound HTTP bodies protect credential placement, explicit rehome trust and bounded telemetry.

cases.title: sends an immediate authenticated heartbeat without putting credentials in the URL
cases.reason: The outbound request authenticates through its header, sends immediately and never includes the bearer credential in the URL.

cases.title: advertises per-host drain only when its dedicated trust boundary is configured
cases.reason: Per-host-drain protocol advertisement depends on the dedicated audience/service-account trust pair, not unrelated configuration.

cases.title: reports the complete enforced connection ledger for a limited cell
cases.reason: The actual heartbeat body includes the full bounded connection ledger and inclusion watermark for a capped cell.

cases.title: does not start outside an explicitly configured cell role
cases.reason: Missing director configuration or a director-only role prevents creation of the heartbeat client.

rationale: Independent numerical expectations protect quantiles, bounded reservoirs and separate acquisition-failure metrics.

cases.title: reports nothing before the first hold
cases.reason: An empty accumulator has no invented duration or count before acquisition.

cases.title: places p95 at the nearest rank for every window size
cases.reason: Independent integer nearest-rank expectations cover reversed samples at every window size from one through 400.

cases.title: ignores a hold that is not a finite, non-negative duration
cases.reason: NaN, infinity and negative holds do not enter the duration reservoir.

cases.title: keeps the most recent holds once the reservoir is full
cases.reason: A full 2048-sample reservoir retains recent durations rather than unbounded history.

cases.title: resets the window on consume so each flush reports its own holds
cases.reason: Consume resets duration state so the next flush contains only new acquisitions.

cases.title: counts failed acquisitions in a window that recorded no holds
cases.reason: Failed acquisitions appear even in a window without a successful hold.

cases.title: reports failed acquisitions alongside the holds that did succeed
cases.reason: Unavailable-lock counts coexist with successful duration samples without replacing them.

cases.title: ignores a failure count that is not a positive number
cases.reason: Invalid and nonpositive failure counts do not inflate diagnostics.

cases.title: resets failed acquisitions on consume
cases.reason: Consume resets failure counters independently of duration data.

cases.title: reports a p99 per hold site
cases.reason: Per-site p99 calculations distinguish inventory, assignment and rehome-target lock populations.

cases.title: names the site of the longest hold and reports rehome target rows apart
cases.reason: The longest hold retains its site and rehome target-row acquisitions remain separately counted.

rationale: Driver and store boundaries protect timeout scope, NOWAIT telemetry and maintenance/request lanes; complementary PostgreSQL suites exercise actual locks.

cases.title: keeps the request bound strictly inside the pool default
cases.reason: The request lock budget is positive and strictly below the pool default, preserving a bounded request queue.

cases.title: restores the pool default before the next statement in the transaction
cases.reason: The PostgreSQL transaction driver restores SET LOCAL before subsequent statements rather than leaking the shorter bound.

cases.title: restores the pool default when the bounded lock itself times out
cases.reason: An actual simulated driver lock timeout still restores the transaction default on the error path.

cases.title: rejects a lock bound that is not a positive whole number of milliseconds
cases.reason: Invalid fractional, zero, negative and nonfinite millisecond bounds fail before SQL execution.

cases.title: skips the timeout for a NOWAIT lock, which never queues
cases.reason: NOWAIT skips SET LOCAL because its refusal already avoids queueing.

cases.title: skips the timeout outside a transaction, where SET LOCAL cannot survive
cases.reason: Autocommit execution skips SET LOCAL because its scope cannot span the lock query.

cases.title: ignores the timeout on SQLite, which has no SET LOCAL
cases.reason: SQLite executes the lock operation without unsupported PostgreSQL timeout syntax.

cases.title: never lets a request path take the unbounded wait
cases.reason: Actual store request entrypoints all pass a bounded inventory-lock option.

cases.title: keeps the pool default when a sweep re-enters placement
cases.reason: A sweep that re-enters placement keeps the pool default instead of inheriting request timing.

cases.title: sends the sweep that re-enters placement down the unbounded lane
cases.reason: The reentrant sweep explicitly selects the unbounded maintenance lane at the store boundary.

cases.title: records the hold on the PostgreSQL transaction path
cases.reason: Measured PostgreSQL transactions report lock acquisition through commit to the duration accumulator.

cases.title: reports a NOWAIT deferral that rolled its transaction back
cases.reason: A NOWAIT refusal remains counted when its transaction rolls back.

cases.title: counts an expired bounded wait apart from a NOWAIT deferral
cases.reason: A bounded timeout increments a different metric from an intentional NOWAIT deferral.

cases.title: records a target-row hold under its own site without appending a lock clause
cases.reason: An already locked target-row query is not given a second lock clause and retains its distinct hold site.

cases.title: records no hold for a PostgreSQL transaction that took no measured lock
cases.reason: Transactions with no measured lock emit no fabricated hold sample.

cases.title: reports how long the inventory lock was held to COMMIT
cases.reason: A real SQLite transaction records the elapsed inventory-lock hold through commit.

cases.title: reports neither a retry nor an exhaustion when NOWAIT finds the lock held
cases.reason: NOWAIT contention avoids retry/exhaustion telemetry intended for retryable transaction failures.

cases.title: takes the inventory NOWAIT and skips the tick instead of queueing
cases.reason: The actual sweep tick skips held inventory rather than joining a lock queue.

cases.title: says nothing on a tick that skipped no candidate
cases.reason: A tick without a skipped candidate emits no misleading deferral diagnostic.

rationale: Held real rows and parallel activity protect per-cell lock scope and exact counters; assertion failures now always release the lock holder.

cases.title: waits only on the pinned cell row while refreshing a sticky assignment
cases.reason: A real held last-cell row and observed waiter distinguish per-cell locking from a fleet-wide lock; release and refresh-task draining now run in finally if assertions fail.

cases.title: keeps a cell reservation exact under concurrent same-cell activity
cases.reason: Six parallel hosts acquire and release actual activity leases while persisted per-cell reservation totals remain exact.

rationale: Real HTTP/WebSocket and SQLite paths prove phone admission/confirmation. Replaced two SQL inventories with persisted basis, lease, renewal and replay outcomes; retained semantic query budgets.

cases.title: acts only while the cell is in reserve mode, so admitMode=db or a dead-man trip turns it off
cases.reason: Real switch/dead-man state selects memory admission only in reserve mode.

cases.title: admits a seated phone resume from one device read and writes no activity lease
cases.reason: A real device resume uses one device read and no activity lease; the query budget now matches the semantic device read rather than a complete SQL string inventory.

cases.title: keeps the database path statement for statement while phonePath is db
cases.reason: Replaced copied SQL statements with durable assertions for the accepted connection basis and confirmation/splice leases on the database path.

cases.title: closes a revoked or expired device 4401 and never tries it as an invite
cases.reason: Revoked and expired device credentials close with 4401 without invite fallback; semantic query matching keeps the one-read contract independent of SQL formatting.

cases.title: closes 4503 when the device read fails, without trying the invite path
cases.reason: A failed device lookup returns 4503 and cannot be misclassified as an absent device/invite.

cases.title: falls through to the invite path only when no device row matches
cases.reason: Only a genuinely absent device falls through to the real invite path.

cases.title: answers a phone whose host has no seat here from one assignment read
cases.reason: Missing or remote host seats use one assignment read and return the appropriate routing answer; the read matcher no longer copies all SQL columns.

cases.title: takes the database path for a phone whose switch turned off during its device read
cases.reason: A flag change during the awaited device read chooses the current database admission path.

cases.title: confirms from the memory basis with one fresh read, renewing a device due for it
cases.reason: A memory confirm performs one fresh device read and persists a due renewal; semantic read matching preserves the budget while allowing SQL evolution.

cases.title: answers renewed:true with the stored expiry when renewal is not due, or its write fails
cases.reason: A renewal not due and a failed renewal write both return the stored expiry without inventing a successful extension.

cases.title: confirms from memory after the switch turned off between accept and confirm, taking no lease
cases.reason: An accepted memory basis remains sufficient after the flag turns off, without acquiring a database lease.

cases.title: replays a stored answer after its splice closed, and drops the basis itself
cases.reason: A committed confirm answer replays after splice closure and the consumed memory basis is discarded.

cases.title: answers a grace-version confirm renewed:false with its expiry unchanged, as today
cases.reason: A grace-version credential preserves its expiry and reports renewed:false under the real memory confirm path.

cases.title: answers every device change since the accept read as the database confirm does
cases.reason: Independent device changes are compared through actual database and memory confirmation implementations, exposing inconsistent authorization or expiry answers.

cases.title: sends a confirm with no memory basis to the database, which holds none either
cases.reason: A missing memory basis falls back to durable confirmation, which also refuses when no basis exists.

cases.title: does not count a lease release that failed after a committed confirm as a failed confirm
cases.reason: A lease-release failure after committed confirmation does not turn success into a failed-confirm metric.

cases.title: keeps the database confirm statement for statement while phonePath is db
cases.reason: Replaced copied SQL inventory with persisted expiry, complete durable confirm result, idempotent replay and confirmation-only lease release assertions.

cases.title: finishes an in-flight confirm on its memory basis after ${name}, writing and leaking no lease
cases.reason: The three rollback modes each finish an already accepted memory confirm without writing or leaking a lease; read budgets use semantic SQL matching.

cases.title: rides out a database outage: splices keep forwarding, new work fails cleanly and recovers
cases.reason: A live splice keeps forwarding during database outage while new work fails cleanly, then recovers and drops expected outage audit work.
