rationale: Fake-time streak/partition decisions and the actual shadow poller protect network classification and safe sample denominators.

cases.title: calls a cell dead only after a continuous failing streak of 45 s
cases.reason: Fake time requires a continuous 45-second failing streak before dead classification.

cases.title: needs a failure within the last 5 s: a frozen director has no verdict until it polls again
cases.reason: A poll gap longer than five seconds suspends the verdict and starts fresh evidence rather than trusting stale observations.

cases.title: resets on any answer from the cell
cases.reason: Any response resets the failing streak, regardless of the returned status.

cases.title: never decides from fewer than ${CELL_POLL_DEAD_MIN_POLLED} polled cells
cases.reason: Fewer than six actually sampled cells cannot establish a dead-cell verdict.

cases.title: withholds when more than a third of the fleet fails at once: this director, not the cells
cases.reason: A fleet with more than one-third failures withholds verdicts as a likely director-side partition.

cases.title: withholds when half or more of the cell's region fails: a cross-region partition
cases.reason: A region with at least half its cells failing withholds a local dead-cell verdict.

cases.title: a staggered partition never judges its first cell dead: young streaks count as failing
cases.reason: Young failing streaks count toward partition protection, preventing staggered failures from condemning the earliest cell.

cases.title: forgets cells no longer listed
cases.reason: Removing a cell clears its historical reachability state.

cases.title: counts timeouts, connection failures and load-balancer 502/503/504 as unanswered
cases.reason: Actual poller fetch boundaries classify timeouts, connection failures and load-balancer 502/503/504 as unanswered.

cases.title: treats any status the cell itself sends as alive: 401, 404, 500
cases.reason: Cell-originated 401, 404 and 500 responses count as answers rather than network death.

cases.title: does not blame a cell for a token this director cannot mint
cases.reason: A local token-mint failure cannot be attributed to a remote cell outage.

cases.title: counts only cells that served a feed: legacy 404 rows neither fill the sample nor dilute it
cases.reason: Only cells that have served a feed enter the sample denominator; legacy 404 rows do not dilute it.

cases.title: a director restarted during a lone outage still judges the dead cell: the candidate is always sampled
cases.reason: A restarted director samples its candidate even without prior feed history, preserving lone-outage recovery.

cases.title: a partition that began before the restart withholds: the candidate is its region's only sample
cases.reason: A candidate that is its region's only post-restart sample retains the regional partition guard.

cases.title: counts no cell without capacity, the candidate included
cases.reason: Cells without configured capacity, including the candidate, do not enter a verdict sample.

cases.title: logs every withheld verdict, sample included, once a minute per cell, for the alert
cases.reason: Withheld verdict logs include their evidence sample and obey a per-cell one-minute limit.

rationale: Actual JWT/WebSocket proof, stalled database pools and capacity ledgers establish memory admission and reconnect/drain races.

cases.title: answers a director dry run only while reserveDryRun is on, and books nothing either way
cases.reason: Real reserve endpoints dry-run only when enabled and leave booking units unchanged in either mode.

cases.title: connects a booked host, and only at its booked epoch, without a database read
cases.reason: JWT/WebSocket proof admits only the booked identity and epoch while the PostgreSQL pool is stalled, proving database-free admission.

cases.title: lets a host that just left rejoin at the same epoch from memory
cases.reason: A recently closed host rejoins its remembered epoch from memory without a new booking.

cases.title: keeps today’s path when the switch is off, even for a booking made while it was on
cases.reason: A booking created while enabled cannot bypass the ordinary database path after the switch turns off.

cases.title: demotes exactly the seat a director names, and repeats are one demotion
cases.reason: Director demotion names one exact seat and repeated requests do not schedule multiple closes.

cases.title: repairs at once the seat a director names when no session backs it
cases.reason: An unbacked seat is repaired immediately on a director report and diagnostics avoid raw host identifiers.

cases.title: leaves a seat no session backs once two sweeps in a row find it, with no director asking
cases.reason: Two consecutive independent sweeps remove an unbacked seat without a director request.

cases.title: lists again a live session the feed lost, once two sweeps in a row find it
cases.reason: Two sweeps restore a live session missing from the seat feed rather than leaving it invisible.

cases.title: repairs nothing for a seat that one sweep finds unbacked and is gone by the next
cases.reason: A seat disappearing between sweeps is not repaired from stale evidence.

cases.title: keeps a session that reconnected while its drained predecessor was still closing
cases.reason: A reconnect arriving while its drained predecessor closes survives with the current generation.

cases.title: stays on the live session when the same identity connects afresh each turn
cases.reason: Repeated fresh connections for the same identity retain the actual live session and monotonically current generation.

cases.title: leaves a drained seat to its drain grace instead of the shorter demotion close
cases.reason: A draining seat follows its longer drain grace rather than the demotion-close timeout.

cases.title: gives every booking unit back when the cell starts to drain
cases.reason: Starting cell drain releases every outstanding booking unit.

cases.title: takes no demotion on a database-mode cell
cases.reason: A database-mode cell rejects reserve demotion instead of mutating ordinary admission state.

cases.title: ends a demotion with its socket, so the host booked back later is an ordinary seat
cases.reason: Closing the demoted socket ends its demotion so a later booking creates an ordinary seat.

cases.title: refuses a booked upgrade at the hard cap and leaves the feed units and bookings as they were
cases.reason: At the hard cap an upgrade is refused without consuming its booking or changing feed units.

cases.title: never crosses the hard cap under seeded bookings, hellos, rebooks and closes
cases.reason: A deterministic 240-operation sequence reaches capacity and never exceeds the hard cap across booking, rebooking, hello and close races.

rationale: Independent capacity/token/epoch examples exercise the real in-memory reservation state machine.

cases.title: books up to the capacity and answers full past it
cases.reason: Independent capacity-two inputs fill the booking cap and expired bookings free capacity.

cases.title: refuses past the intake budget and refills at the configured rate
cases.reason: The intake token bucket refuses excess fresh bookings and refills at the configured fake-clock rate.

cases.title: answers seated-newer when the host is seated or booked at an equal or higher epoch
cases.reason: Equal or newer seated/booked epochs reject stale replacements.

cases.title: lets a sticky re-booking skip the intake bucket but never the cap
cases.reason: Sticky rebooking bypasses intake throttling while remaining bounded by hard capacity.

cases.title: answers ok for a sticky re-booking of a host already seated at that epoch, booking nothing
cases.reason: An already seated sticky epoch succeeds without allocating an additional booking unit.

cases.title: consumes a booking once, only at its own epoch, and releases its unit
cases.reason: Only the exact booked epoch consumes its unit, and consumption is once-only.

cases.title: answers off outside reserve mode, draining while draining, and dry runs book nothing
cases.reason: Database mode, drain and dry-run flags return their public outcomes without reserving capacity.

cases.title: hands a lower-epoch booking unit to its successor rather than taking a second
cases.reason: A newer epoch inherits its lower-epoch booking unit instead of counting the host twice.

cases.title: hands a booking unit to the host upgrade, so the host counts once until its hello
cases.reason: A booked upgrade transfers its unit until hello, preserving a single counted host across handoff.

rationale: Actual client serialization and response parsing protect batching, credentials and fail-closed malformed replies.

cases.title: batches a cell’s bookings into one request and maps each answer back
cases.reason: The real client batches two bookings and a dry run into the authenticated production URL/body and maps distinct replies back to their identities.

cases.title: reads every item as unreachable when the cell fails or answers out of shape
cases.reason: HTTP failure, malformed payloads and mismatched result counts classify each requested booking as unreachable.

rationale: Actual PostgreSQL leases and delayed trips protect live-control rollback, limited concurrency and grouped writes; real latency is intentional.

cases.title: re-registers every memory-admitted control, ten flips in a row
cases.reason: Ten real memory/database mode cycles persist every control lease without closing the live sockets.

cases.title: keeps re-registration to a third of the pool and one cell-row write per tick, at 170 ms a trip
cases.reason: Real delayed PostgreSQL round trips with nine hosts keep registration concurrency to three of ten pool slots and combine cell-row writes per tick.

rationale: Real connection proofs and durable lease writes distinguish permanent refusal from outage/race retries and protect rollback/dead-man behavior.

cases.title: registers every memory-admitted control without disconnecting any, matching the seat report
cases.reason: Real handshakes admitted from memory become durable control leases after rollback while their sockets and seat report stay consistent.

cases.title: closes with 4409 a control whose row never names this cell, after every retry
cases.reason: A permanently mismatched assignment closes with 4409 after the retry budget.

cases.title: gives up on a refusal from a database that answered, as on a row naming another seat
cases.reason: A database response explicitly refusing registration is distinguished from an unavailable database and eventually closes the control.

cases.title: retries a stalled database for as long as the control is open, and closes nobody for it
cases.reason: Transient 57P01 failures remain retryable beyond the refusal budget and recover without disconnecting the host.

cases.title: retries a lease insert that lost a race (23505) instead of counting it as a refusal
cases.reason: A raced lease insert raising 23505 remains retryable and eventually succeeds rather than becoming a policy refusal.

cases.title: never lets the switch file take the connections hellos and renewals need
cases.reason: Independent pool-size examples bound rollback concurrency so hello and renewal connections remain available.

cases.title: takes its flip-back pace from the switch file
cases.reason: A switch-file pace of one controls the real registration worker, not just the exposed calculation.

cases.title: leases a control whose proof lands after the flip, though memory admitted its hello
cases.reason: A proof arriving after the mode flip still receives its required durable control lease.

cases.title: writes an admit-effective row only while its switch says reserve, plus one db write on the way out
cases.reason: A never-enabled reserve cell performs no effective-mode write; leaving reserve writes database mode once.

cases.title: flips itself back to db when no placing director has been in touch for the dead-man window
cases.reason: Fake-clock staggered director contacts reset the dead-man timer; expiration latches database mode, registers controls and persists effective mode.

rationale: Real HTTP middleware protects dedicated trust, route availability and complete seat identity.

cases.title: books for a director holding the rehome credential and refuses everyone else
cases.reason: Real Hono requests enforce the dedicated rehome credential and request schema before invoking a booking callback.

cases.title: is absent on a director and on a cell without the rehome pair
cases.reason: Director-only role and incomplete cell trust configuration do not register reserve routes.

cases.title: demotes only a fully named seat
cases.reason: Demotion rejects incomplete identity/version data and passes the exact joined-at seat identity to the callback.

rationale: Distinct session diagnostic reasons and actual two-sweep confirmation state provide focused failure diagnosis beyond blackbox repair flows.

cases.title: names why no live session backs a seat, and nothing when one does
cases.reason: Closed, missing-socket and wrong-generation sessions produce distinct diagnostic causes; a matching live session produces none.

cases.title: confirms only what two sweeps in a row found, at most once per sweep interval
cases.reason: The actual two-sweep state machine confirms persistent drift only, clears repaired candidates and limits confirmations to one per sweep interval.
